If I could make one change to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, I would get rid of that new swipe-down gesture to summon Siri AI. There are already plenty of existing ways to invoke Siri, and there's no need to break my muscle memory of opening Notification Center on my iPhone and iPad.

Meanwhile, on the Mac side, macOS 27 Golden Gate is almost entirely good news. Even at the end of August, new betas are still adding welcome changes. However, before macOS 27 ships next month, there's still one change I'd like to see.

macOS 27 Golden Gate makes MacBook battery percentage harder to read

macOS 27 Golden Gate redesigned the battery control in the menu bar. By default, the percentage is not displayed — there's only a battery-shaped visual indicator icon.

In this state, it looks fine. I do the same on my iPhone, turning off the percentage display and using the same battery indicator. However, on the Mac, I've always preferred to display the percentage.

If you turn on the "Show Percentage" option in macOS 27 Golden Gate, the number will appear inside the battery icon. I think this is to keep it consistent with how iOS 27 displays it on the iPhone.

Putting the percentage inside the battery icon on the iPhone was Apple's way of dealing with space density issues of cramming everything to the right of the notch or Dynamic Island. As for the Mac, even in the menu bar, I don't have this screen space issue.

I've been running macOS 27 Golden Gate on my 15-inch MacBook Air since the first developer beta dropped. I've found myself paying less attention to the battery percentage in general, because to my eyes, it's become less readable.

I hope Apple will reconsider this design decision later, especially if it bothers more users. In the meantime, I've at least solved this problem for myself.

I used Codex to create a simple menu bar widget that displays the current battery status and percentage clearly and reliably, matching the visual clarity I'd expect. If you think this might help you too, you can click here to download and install it for free.
